SECTION 4 — SCOPE OF SERVICES
CHANGE MANAGEMENT AND WORKFORCE TRANSITION
Integrated Depot and Rolling Stock Maintenance System (IDRMS)

4.1 Background
4.1.1 The Operator runs a network of 6 depots and 3 permanent way sites across the country and will replace its legacy maintenance management application with the IDRMS platform. The programme will run over a period of 14 months from contract award, delivered in 3 waves aligned to depot readiness.
4.1.2 The transition affects approximately 2,400 employees, comprising maintenance technicians, depot supervisors, rolling stock engineers, materials controllers, permanent way crews and the central maintenance planning office. Frontline staff work a rotating shift roster and have limited access to desktop computers during the working day.

4.2 Change Management Requirements
4.2.1 The Contractor shall develop a Change Management Strategy and an integrated change management plan covering the full programme lifecycle, including the change governance approach and the change management team structure to be deployed.
4.2.2 The Contractor shall conduct a change impact assessment covering each affected depot and the central planning office. The Operator anticipates the assessment will address 7 business units. The impact register shall record process, role, system and industrial-relations impacts, and shall be validated with the relevant union representatives.
4.2.3 The Contractor shall carry out stakeholder analysis and produce a stakeholder engagement plan, giving specific attention to union stakeholders, depot leadership and the shift-based frontline population.
4.2.4 The Contractor shall establish and activate a change agent network drawing nominated change champions from every depot, and shall provide the network with an activation session, a toolkit and ongoing coaching support.
4.2.5 The Contractor shall conduct change readiness assessments before each of the deployment waves, and shall report results with recommended mitigations to the Programme Steering Committee.
4.2.6 The Contractor shall develop a communications plan and produce the associated communications collaterals. Given the shift-based workforce, collaterals shall include depot noticeboard posters, shift briefing packs, toolbox talk cards and short video messages from the Chief Operating Officer suitable for viewing on personal mobile devices.
4.2.7 The Contractor shall provide CM status reporting to the Programme Management Office on a weekly basis, maintain the change RAID log, and support the monthly Programme Steering Committee.

4.3 Training Requirements
4.3.1 The Contractor shall develop a training plan and shall design and deliver role-based training for all affected employees. The Operator has identified 9 training modules spanning work order management, asset registry, materials requisition, planned maintenance scheduling, defect reporting, safety certification, mobile inspection, reporting and system administration.
4.3.2 Training shall be delivered through instructor-led sessions at each depot. Classes shall be capped at not more than 15 participants per session to accommodate hands-on practice at the terminals.
4.3.3 The Contractor shall deliver train-the-trainer sessions to build a sustainable internal training capability, and shall produce user guides, quick reference guides and micro-learning assets suitable for mobile viewing.
4.3.4 All training materials shall be produced in 2 languages.
4.3.5 The Contractor shall provide UAT support training ahead of each wave.

4.4 Deployment and Post Go-Live
4.4.1 The Contractor shall provide hypercare support for 3 months following each wave go-live, including on-site floorwalking at depots during the first two weeks of each wave.
4.4.2 The Contractor shall run user adoption clinics at each depot during hypercare and shall establish expert user groups to sustain capability after the Contractor demobilises.
4.4.3 The Contractor shall produce a post-implementation review report for each wave and shall define the adoption measurement approach, including the success measures and the reporting cadence.
4.4.4 The Contractor shall produce a handover plan and a change sustenance plan transferring ongoing change and training responsibilities to the Operator's Learning and Development function.

4.5 Optional Scope
4.5.1 Tenderers shall price the following as an option: an orientation programme for the Operator's incoming digital maintenance team, covering agile ways of working and the target operating model.
4.5.2 Tenderers shall price as an option the development of system demo videos covering each of the training modules.
